title: Pricing tier rename + cap rebalance: launch coordination & comms playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Coordinate rollout for the pricing tier rename and cap rebalance initiative: rename three SKUs, redistribute token limits across tiers, migrate existing entitlements on invoices, update Console/UIs, update billing ingestion, and prepare customer and sales communications. This ticket is the cross-functional orchestration playbook to ensure coherent rollout, minimize customer confusion, and align support, finance, and sales for migration assistance.
checklist: Finalize new tier names and mapping table (old -> new) and publish to internal doc
Sign-off on cap rebalance numbers from Finance and Pricing (token and request rate caps)
Billing ingestion changes implemented and end-to-end tested in staging
Console UI strings updated and L10n pass booked
SDK/backwards-compat notes and update for client libs published
Flag-based rollout implemented with opt-out window for affected customers
Customer migration script validated on shadow invoices and a small pilot cohort
Sales enablement materials completed: one-pager, FAQ, migration playbook
Support runbook published with escalation path to PM and Billing Ops
Release notes drafted and coordinated across Engineering, Docs, and Legal
comments: 2026-02-10 | Aisha Patel: Kickoff — documented scope and initial stakeholder list. Added Finance, Billing Ops, Console, SDK, Support, Legal, and Sales enablement owners. Tentative launch target: 2026-03-01.

2026-02-11 | Diego Torres (Billing): Confirmed billing ingestion schema change will be additive; mapping table for old SKU->new SKU required to preserve invoice continuity. Billing Ops requests downtime window on 2026-03-01 02:00-04:00 UTC.

2026-02-12 | Marina Liu (Engineering): ENG-11422 implementing cap rebalance logic and flags. Completed unit tests; integration with feature-flag service in progress. Need product acceptance on edge-case rounding rules.
2026-02-13 | Ethan Cole (PM, assignee): Drafted migration mapping and customer segmentation for pilot (50 accounts: low-, mid-, high-usage). Added pilot schedule to checklist.

2026-02-14 | Priya Shah (Sales): Request for 2-week advanced notice for enterprise customers and pre-approved email copy for account execs. Also requested competitive FAQ comparing new tiers to legacy packaging.
2026-02-16 | QA Lead (Jon Park): End-to-end test plan uploaded to Confluence. Found two console label translation regressions — DES-4231 assigned to Design.
2026-02-17 | Support (Karen O'Neill): Support runbook draft looks good. Need sample refund/credit templates for customers who will be negatively impacted by stricter caps.
2026-02-18 | Aisha Patel: Updated release notes draft and added billing migration checklist. Set go/no-go review meeting for 2026-02-25.
2026-02-18 | Legal (Marco Ruiz): Quick review complete. No outstanding compliance concerns; recommend conservative language in public comms to avoid implying retroactive billing changes.
acceptance_criteria: All dependent engineering tickets (ENG-11422, ENG-11988) are merged to main and deployed to staging
Billing migration script runs cleanly on shadow invoices and pilot cohort with no invoice number collisions
Console UI shows new tier names in staging and passes visual QA and L10n checks
Customer-facing release notes and sales one-pager signed off by Legal and Sales Ops
Support has triage/escalation playbook and templates for credit/refund scenarios
Feature flag exists to toggle mapping logic and is testable per-customer
Pilot customers completed migration successfully and no critical incidents reported within 72 hours
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Internal dry-run (2026-02-20): Run migration script against staging shadow invoices, update console staging strings, and run support playbook walkthrough
Phase 1 — Pilot (2026-02-22 to 2026-02-26): Migrate 50 pilot customers with Sales & Account Execs on standby; monitor billing, logs, SLOs, and support tickets
Phase 2 — Gradual roll (2026-03-01): Enable mapping for 25% of customers at 02:00 UTC with billing maintenance window; monitor for 6 hours, then increase to 100% over 24 hours if healthy
Phase 3 — Public comms (2026-03-02): Publish release notes, updated pricing docs, and send segmented emails to customers with migration details and opt-out window instructions
Phase 4 — Post-launch (2026-03-03 to 2026-03-10): Collect telemetry for regressions, capture CSAT from migrated customers, and queue any follow-up tickets for cap adjustments
